I'll look at the codebase to understand what "follow/unfollow" involves here before writing a test plan.

Read the module. Here's the plan.

## Surface under test

| Route | Guard | Handler → Service |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /profiles/:username/follow` | `AuthMiddleware` (`profiles/:username/follow`, ALL methods) | `follow(@User('email'), username)` |
| `DELETE /profiles/:username/follow` | same | `unFollow(@User('id'), username)` |
| `GET /profiles/:username` | **none** (public) | `findProfile(@User('id'), username)` — reads follow state |
| `GET /articles/feed` | `AuthMiddleware` | `findFeed(userId)` — consumes `follows` rows |

Code: `src/profile/profile.service.ts:50-102`, `profile.controller.ts:23-31`, `follows.entity.ts`, `article.service.ts:66-94`.

Note the identity asymmetry: **follow is keyed on email, unfollow on id** (`profile.controller.ts:24` vs `:29`). Every test must exercise both paths, not assume symmetry.

## Harness prerequisites (currently missing)

- `jest.json` `testRegex` is `/src/.*\.(test|spec)\.(ts|tsx|js)$` → tests must live **under `src/`**, and `profile.e2e-spec.ts` would **not** match (`\.` is escaped). Name it `src/profile/profile.e2e.spec.ts`.
- The only existing spec (`src/tag/tag.controller.spec.ts:13`) calls `TypeOrmModule.forRoot()`, which needs a live MySQL + a real `ormconfig.json` (repo only ships `.example`). There is no test DB, no seeding, no truncation between tests.
- Unit layer needs no DB: provide `getRepositoryToken(UserEntity)` / `getRepositoryToken(FollowsEntity)` mocks.
- E2E layer needs a DB decision (see question at the end).

## Layer 1 — service unit tests (`profile.service.spec.ts`)

Mocked `userRepository` / `followsRepository`.

| ID | Case | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| U1 | `follow(email, username)`, no existing row | `followsRepository.save` called with `{followerId, followingId}`; returns `{profile:{…, following:true}}` |
| U2 | `follow` when row already exists | **no** `save` call; still returns `following:true` (idempotent) |
| U3 | `follow` with own username | `HttpException` 400, no `save` |
| U4 | `follow('' , username)` / `follow(email, '')` | 400 — guard at `:51` (unreachable via HTTP; unit-only) |
| U5 | **`follow` with unknown username** | should be **404**; currently `followingUser.email` at `:58` throws `TypeError` on `undefined` → 500 |
| U6 | `unFollow(id, username)` with existing row | `delete({followerId, followingId})` called; `following:false` |
| U7 | `unFollow` when not following | 200, `following:false`, delete affects 0 rows (pin idempotence) |
| U8 | `unFollow` with own id | 400, no delete |
| U9 | `unFollow(0, …)` | falsy-id guard at `:82` fires 400 — assert no valid user can have id `0` |
| U10 | **`unFollow` with unknown username** | should be 404; currently `followingUser.id` at `:88` → 500 |
| U11 | `findProfile(id, username)` following / not following | `following` is exactly `true` / `false`, never `undefined` |
| U12 | **`findProfile(undefined, username)`** (anonymous) | spec wants `following:false`; `if (id)` at `:43` skips the assignment → key **omitted** |
| U13 | **`findProfile(id, 'nobody')`** | should be 404; `:33` returns `undefined` → Nest sends 200 empty body |

## Layer 2 — HTTP e2e (`profile.e2e.spec.ts`, supertest)

Fixtures: users `alice`, `bob`, tokens for both.

| ID | Request | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | `POST /profiles/bob/follow` as alice | 201, body exactly `{profile:{username,bio,image,following:true}}` — no `id`, no `password`, no `email` |
| E2 | Repeat E1 | 201, `following:true`, and **exactly one** row in `follows` |
| E3 | `DELETE /profiles/bob/follow` as alice | 200, `following:false`, zero rows |
| E4 | Repeat E3 | 200, `following:false` (idempotent) |
| E5 | follow → unfollow → follow | final state one row, `following:true` |
| E6 | `POST /profiles/alice/follow` as alice | 400 |
| E7 | `DELETE /profiles/alice/follow` as alice | 400 |
| E8 | follow/unfollow with **no** `Authorization` header | 401 `Not authorized.` |
| E9 | follow/unfollow with **malformed or expired** token | should be 401; `jwt.verify` at `auth.middleware.ts:17` is uncaught → **500** (LESSONS #79) |
| E10 | `Bearer <jwt>` instead of `Token <jwt>` | 201 — scheme word is ignored by design; pin it |
| E11 | follow/unfollow `:username` that does not exist | should be 404; currently 500 (U5/U10 over HTTP) |
| E12 | `GET /profiles/bob` as alice, while following | 200, `following:true` |
| E13 | `GET /profiles/bob` **anonymous** | should be `following:false`; currently key absent (U12) |
| E14 | `GET /profiles/bob` anonymous with a **garbage token** | should be 401 or ignore; `user.decorator.ts:15` `jwt.verify` uncaught → 500 |
| E15 | `GET /profiles/nobody` | should be 404; currently 200 + empty body |
| E16 | `GET /profiles/alice` as alice | 200, `following:false` |
| E17 | Username casing / URL-encoded chars (`GET /profiles/Bob`) | pin whatever collation does — MySQL default is case-insensitive, so `Bob` likely resolves to `bob` |

## Layer 3 — cross-feature integration

Follow state is only meaningful because the feed reads it.

| ID | Case | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | alice follows bob, bob has 2 articles → `GET /articles/feed` | both articles, `articlesCount:2` |
| I2 | alice follows **two** authors → feed | articles from both. `article.service.ts:77` uses `IN (:ids)` not `IN (:...ids)`; array expansion here is driver-dependent — **this test is the one that proves it** |
| I3 | alice unfollows bob → feed | `{articles:[], articlesCount:0}` (the early return at `:69`) |
| I4 | alice follows bob, bob has zero articles → feed | empty list, not an error |
| I5 | feed with `?limit=1&offset=1` while following | `articlesCount` is the **unpaginated** total |
| I6 | after follow, `GET /articles` for bob's article | `author.following` — the spec field; check whether the article path produces it at all |

## Data integrity / concurrency

| ID | Case | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | Two simultaneous `POST …/follow` | `follows.entity.ts` has **no unique index** on `(followerId, followingId)`; the check-then-save at `:62-68` is a TOCTOU race → duplicate rows. Assert one row; expect failure |
| C2 | Follow bob, then `DELETE /users/bob@…` (public, unguarded), then `GET /articles/feed` | `followerId`/`followingId` are plain `int` columns with no FK → orphan rows survive. Pin the behaviour |
| C3 | Follow bob, then bob changes email via `PUT /user` | follow still works by id; **unfollow-by-id still works, follow-by-email now resolves differently** — worth pinning given the `Object.assign` bug (LESSONS #112) |

## Defects this plan is designed to surface

U5/U10/E11 (404→500), U12/E13 (`following` omitted for anonymous), U13/E15 (404→200-empty), E9/E14 (401→500), C1 (no unique constraint), plus I2 as a verification. Write these as failing tests first and mark them — don't soften the assertion to match current behaviour, or the suite will lock the bugs in.

## Out of scope

`ProfileService.findAll()` and `findOne()` (lines 19-28) are not wired to any route; `findOne` also dereferences `user.id` before its null check. Worth a ticket, not a test.
